hints: Look past the -CO2H group and focus on what is different, one molecule has only an acid, one has an alcohol as well, and one has a ketone as well.
Remember all carboxylic acids fizz with NaHCO3, so that test cannot separate three acids, while warm acidified dichromate turns green only with the secondary alcohol.
To separate the remaining simple acid from the keto-acid, think about which reagent gives an orange precipitate specifically with C=O of aldehydes and ketones.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional groups in each liquid**

All three liquids are colourless acids, so look carefully at the rest of the molecule.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is propanoic acid, acid only. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$ is 2-hydroxypropanoic acid, acid plus secondary alcohol. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCO}_2\text{H}$ is 2-oxopropanoic acid, acid plus ketone.

**Check why test with NaHCO3 is useless here**

Carboxylic acids react with hydrogencarbonate to give effervescence:
$$\text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{HCO}_3^- \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2^- + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Since all three contain $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, all three will fizz. This cannot identify anyone, so options A and B fail at test 1.

**Use warm acidified dichromate to find the alcohol**

Warm $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}/\text{H}^+$ oxidises primary and secondary alcohols (orange to green) but does not oxidise carboxylic acids or ketones.

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$ has an oxidisable secondary $\text{-CH(OH)-}$ group, so only it turns orange to green. The other two stay orange.

**Use 2,4-DNPH to find the ketone**

2,4-DNPH gives an orange-yellow precipitate with the C=O of aldehydes and ketones, but no reaction with acids or alcohols alone.

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{COCO}_2\text{H}$ has a ketone C=O, so only it gives the precipitate. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is negative to both tests. This pair of results uniquely identifies all three.

options.A: Incorrect. NaHCO3 gives CO2 effervescence with all three carboxylic acids, so test 1 gives no separation. Although 2,4-DNPH would pick out the keto-acid, the alcohol-acid and simple acid would still be confused.
options.B: Incorrect. NaHCO3 again reacts with all three, so it is not discriminating. Tollens reagent is also unsuitable because it oxidises aldehydes only, and neither the ketone nor the simple acid will give a silver mirror, so two liquids would both be negative.
options.C: Correct. Warm acidified dichromate is positive (green) only for CH3CH(OH)CO2H due to its secondary alcohol. 2,4-DNPH is positive (orange precipitate) only for CH3COCO2H due to its ketone. CH3CH2CO2H is negative to both, giving three unique patterns.
options.D: Incorrect. Warm acidified dichromate correctly isolates the hydroxy-acid, but Tollens reagent fails as test 2. Tollens is positive for aldehydes, not ketones, so both CH3CH2CO2H and CH3COCO2H give no reaction and cannot be distinguished.
